title: Using Codex to fix repetitive trivia rounds in my game
author: Patient_Tennis_9793
selftext:
I’m a UNC student and I made Who’s Bluffing with Codex. It’s ten trivia questions, but you also choose how sure you are. Confident mistakes cost more points.

One player picked History and got four Australia/New Zealand questions in a row. Fair complaint. I used Codex to change how rounds select questions, with limits on repeated subjects, eras and regions. We checked the change across 6,000 simulated History rounds.

The harder question is whether a balanced mix actually feels varied. How do you test that in games with random content?

There’s also a Memes pack, and you can challenge a friend to the exact same ten questions. Free, no accounts or ads.

[https://whosbluffing.com/play?pack=memes](https://whosbluffing.com/play?pack=memes)
